<result>## Quick Start

```typescript
import { Agent } from "@earendil-works/pi-agent-core";
import { createModels } from "@earendil-works/pi-ai";
import { anthropicProvider } from "@earendil-works/pi-ai/providers/anthropic";

const models = createModels();
models.setProvider(anthropicProvider());
const model = models.getModel("anthropic", "claude-sonnet-4-6");
if (!model) throw new Error("Model not found");

const agent = new Agent({
  initialState: {
    systemPrompt: "You are a helpful assistant.",
    model,
  },
  streamFn: models.streamSimple.bind(models),
});

agent.subscribe((event) => {
  if (event.type === "message_update" && event.assistantMessageEvent.type === "text_delta") {
    // Stream just the new text chunk
    process.stdout.write(event.assistantMessageEvent.delta);
  }
});

await agent.prompt("Hello!");
```

-----
## Agent Options

```typescript
const agent = new Agent({
  // Initial state. systemPrompt and tools become the leading system message
  // unless messages already starts with one.
  initialState: {
    systemPrompt: string,
    model: Model<any>,
    thinkingLevel: "off" | "minimal" | "low" | "medium" | "high" | "xhigh" | "max",
    tools: AgentTool<any>[],
    messages: AgentMessage[],
  },

  // Convert AgentMessage[] to LLM Message[] (required for custom message types)
  convertToLlm: (messages) => messages.filter(...),

  // Transform context before convertToLlm (for pruning, compaction)
  transformContext: async (messages, signal) => pruneOldMessages(messages),

  // Steering mode: "one-at-a-time" (default) or "all"
  steeringMode: "one-at-a-time",

  // Follow-up mode: "one-at-a-time" (default) or "all"
  followUpMode: "one-at-a-time",

  // Required stream function. Receives a TranscriptContext: the prompt and tools
  // are in the transcript's system messages, not on the context.
  streamFn: models.streamSimple.bind(models),

  // Session ID for provider caching
  sessionId: "session-123",

  // How requests identify the app to providers (pi-ai ClientIdentity), merged over
  // DEFAULT_AGENT_IDENTITY ({ attribution: PI_ATTRIBUTION }: provider attribution headers name pi).
  // Pass your app's attribution, or null to send none.
  identity: { attribution: { name: "my-app", url: "https://my-app.example" } },

  // Dynamic API key resolution (for expiring OAuth tokens)
  getApiKey: async (provider) => refreshToken(),

  // Tool execution mode: "parallel" (default) or "sequential"
  toolExecution: "parallel",

  // Preflight each tool call after args are validated. Can block execution.
  beforeToolCall: async ({ toolCall, args, context }) => {
    if (toolCall.name === "bash") {
      return { block: true, reason: "bash is disabled", terminate: true };
    }
  },

  // Postprocess each tool result before final tool events are emitted.
  afterToolCall: async ({ toolCall, result, isError, context }) => {
    if (toolCall.name === "notify_done" && !isError) {
      return { terminate: true };
    }
    if (!isError) {
      return { details: { ...result.details, audited: true } };
    }
  },

  // Rebuild finalized context immediately before every provider request.
  prepareRequest: async ({ context }, signal) => {
    return { context: { ...context, messages: await loadCanonicalMessages(signal) } };
  },

  // Finalize a completed turn before turn_end is emitted.
  // `continue` ensures one next request; existing tool/queue scheduling can satisfy it.
  // `end` ends this run after turn_end without polling queues.
  finishTurn: async ({ message, toolResults }, signal) => {
    return shouldContinue(message, toolResults) ? { action: "continue" } : undefined;
  },

  // Custom thinking budgets for token-based providers
  thinkingBudgets: {
    minimal: 128,
    low: 512,
    medium: 1024,
    high: 2048,
  },
});
```

-----
## Tools

Define tools using `AgentTool`. `parameters` is any JSON Schema object; built with `@earendil-works/pi-schema`'s builders, it also types `params` (other schemas give `unknown`, `AgentTool<any>` gives `any`):

```typescript
import { obj, str } from "@earendil-works/pi-schema";

const readFileParameters = obj({
  path: str({ description: "File path" }),
});

const readFileTool: AgentTool<typeof readFileParameters> = {
  name: "read_file",
  label: "Read File",  // For UI display
  description: "Read a file's contents",
  parameters: readFileParameters,
  // Override execution mode for this tool (optional).
  // "sequential" forces the entire batch to run one at a time.
  // "parallel" allows concurrent execution with other tool calls.
  // If omitted, the global toolExecution config applies.
  executionMode: "sequential",
  execute: async (toolCallId, params, signal, onUpdate) => {
    const content = await fs.readFile(params.path, "utf-8");

    // Optional: stream progress
    onUpdate?.({ content: [{ type: "text", text: "Reading..." }], details: {} });

    // Optional: add `terminate: true` here to skip the automatic follow-up LLM call
    // when every finalized tool result in the batch does the same.
    return {
      content: [{ type: "text", text: content }],
      details: { path: params.path, size: content.length },
    };
  },
};

agent.state.tools = [readFileTool];
```

### Error Handling

**Throw an error** when a tool fails. Do not return error messages as content.

```typescript
execute: async (toolCallId, params, signal, onUpdate) => {
  if (!fs.existsSync(params.path)) {
    throw new Error(`File not found: ${params.path}`);
  }
  // Return content only on success
  return { content: [{ type: "text", text: "..." }] };
}
```

Thrown errors are caught by the agent and reported to the LLM as tool errors with `isError: true`.

Return `terminate: true` from `execute()`, a blocked `beforeToolCall`, or `afterToolCall` to hint that the agent should stop after the current tool batch. This only takes effect when every finalized tool result in the batch is terminating. The hint is runtime-only; emitted `toolResult` transcript messages remain standard LLM tool results.

### MCP and Codemode

`@earendil-works/pi-mcp` connects to MCP servers and `@earendil-works/pi-codemode` runs model-written JavaScript that calls tools. [examples/mcp-codemode](examples/mcp-codemode) wraps both as `AgentTool`s: one tool per MCP tool, and a `codemode` tool whose scripts call the agent's tools through `runToolCall()`, so `beforeToolCall` and `afterToolCall` apply to those calls too.

/**
 * Preview renderer.
 *
 * Renders the single in-memory file into an iframe.
 *
 * Flicker-free streaming: when content grows by a prefix (the agent appending
 * a chunk), we `document.write()` only the new tail into the live document —
 * the browser renders it progressively without reloading. When content is
 * replaced or reloaded, we reopen the document from scratch.
 *
 * A console-capture script is injected on full renders so `get_console` can
 * read the preview's console output.
 */

import { getFile, onChange } from "./file";

const iframe = document.getElementById("preview-frame") as HTMLIFrameElement;
const reloadBtn = document.getElementById("reload-btn") as HTMLButtonElement;

// --- Console capture ------------------------------------------------------

const consoleMessages: string[] = [];

window.addEventListener("message", (event) => {
	if (event.data?.type === "console") {
		const level = event.data.level ?? "log";
		const args = event.data.args ?? [];
		consoleMessages.push(`[${level}] ${args.join(" ")}`);
	}
});

/** Script written into the document to forward console output + errors. */
const CONSOLE_CAPTURE_SCRIPT = `<script>
(function() {
	var levels = ["log", "info", "warn", "error", "debug"];
	levels.forEach(function(level) {
		var orig = console[level];
		console[level] = function() {
			try {
				parent.postMessage({
					type: "console",
					level: level,
					args: Array.prototype.map.call(arguments, function(a) {
						if (typeof a === "object") {
							try { return JSON.stringify(a); } catch(e) { return String(a); }
						}
						return String(a);
					})
				}, "*");
			} catch(e) {}
			orig.apply(console, arguments);
		};
	});
	window.addEventListener("error", function(e) {
		try {
			parent.postMessage({ type: "console", level: "error", args: [e.message + " (" + e.filename + ":" + e.lineno + ")"] }, "*");
		} catch(err) {}
	});
})();
<\/script>`;

// --- Streaming render state ----------------------------------------------

/** What's currently committed to the live iframe document. */
let committed: { content: string; hasCapture: boolean } | null = null;

/** Write a string into the live iframe document via document.write. */
function writeDoc(html: string): void {
	const doc = iframe.contentDocument;
	if (!doc) return;
	doc.write(html);
}

/** Reopen the document from scratch, optionally with the console capture. */
function openDocument(withCapture: boolean): void {
	const doc = iframe.contentDocument;
	if (!doc) return;
	doc.open();
	if (withCapture) writeDoc(CONSOLE_CAPTURE_SCRIPT);
}

/**
 * Display `content` in the preview.
 *
 * If `content` extends what's already committed (prefix match) and the capture
 * requirement is satisfied, only the new tail is written — no reload, no flicker.
 * Otherwise the document is reopened and fully rewritten.
 */
function display(content: string, needCapture: boolean): void {
	const c = committed;
	const canExtend =
		c !== null &&
		content.length >= c.content.length &&
		content.startsWith(c.content) &&
		(!needCapture || c.hasCapture);

	if (canExtend) {
		writeDoc(content.slice(c!.content.length));
		committed = { content, hasCapture: c!.hasCapture };
		return;
	}

	openDocument(needCapture);
	writeDoc(content || "<!-- empty -->");
	committed = { content, hasCapture: needCapture };
}

// --- Public API -----------------------------------------------------------

/** Render the current file fully (with console capture). */
export function render(): void {
	display(getFile(), true);
}

/**
 * Render a partial (in-progress) version of the file during streaming.
 * No console capture — keeps streaming smooth. Captured on the next full render.
 */
export function renderPartial(html: string): void {
	display(html, false);
}

/** Reset the committed state so the next display() reopens the document. */
export function invalidate(): void {
	committed = null;
}

/** Capture the iframe content as a base64 image. */
export async function getScreenshot(): Promise<string> {

		const iframeDoc = iframe.contentDocument;

		const bodyStyle = iframeDoc.body?.style?.cssText ?? "";
		const computed = iframeDoc.defaultView?.getComputedStyle(iframeDoc.body ?? iframeDoc.documentElement) ?? null;
		const bgColor = computed?.backgroundColor ?? "#ffffff";

/**
 * Preview renderer.
 *
 * Renders the single in-memory file into an iframe.
 *
 * Flicker-free streaming: when content grows by a prefix (the agent appending
 * a chunk), we `document.write()` only the new tail into the live document —
 * the browser renders it progressively without reloading. When content is
 * replaced or reloaded, we reopen the document from scratch.
 *
 * A console-capture script is injected on full renders so `get_console` can
 * read the preview's console output.
 */

import { getFile, onChange } from "./file";

const iframe = document.getElementById("preview-frame") as HTMLIFrameElement;
const reloadBtn = document.getElementById("reload-btn") as HTMLButtonElement;

// --- Console capture ------------------------------------------------------

const consoleMessages: string[] = [];

window.addEventListener("message", (event) => {
	if (event.data?.type === "console") {
		const level = event.data.level ?? "log";
		const args = event.data.args ?? [];
		consoleMessages.push(`[${level}] ${args.join(" ")}`);
	}
});

/** Script written into the document to forward console output + errors. */
const CONSOLE_CAPTURE_SCRIPT = `<script>
(function() {
	var levels = ["log", "info", "warn", "error", "debug"];
	levels.forEach(function(level) {
		var orig = console[level];
		console[level] = function() {
			try {
				parent.postMessage({
					type: "console",
					level: level,
					args: Array.prototype.map.call(arguments, function(a) {
						if (typeof a === "object") {
							try { return JSON.stringify(a); } catch(e) { return String(a); }
						}
						return String(a);
					})
				}, "*");
			} catch(e) {}
			orig.apply(console, arguments);
		};
	});
	window.addEventListener("error", function(e) {
		try {
			parent.postMessage({ type: "console", level: "error", args: [e.message + " (" + e.filename + ":" + e.lineno + ")"] }, "*");
		} catch(err) {}
	});
})();
<\/script>`;

// --- Streaming render state ----------------------------------------------

/** What's currently committed to the live iframe document. */
let committed: { content: string; hasCapture: boolean } | null = null;

/** Write a string into the live iframe document via document.write. */
function writeDoc(html: string): void {
	const doc = iframe.contentDocument;
	if (!doc) return;
	doc.write(html);
}

/** Reopen the document from scratch, optionally with the console capture. */
function openDocument(withCapture: boolean): void {
	const doc = iframe.contentDocument;
	if (!doc) return;
	doc.open();
	if (withCapture) writeDoc(CONSOLE_CAPTURE_SCRIPT);
}

/**
 * Display `content` in the preview.
 *
 * If `content` extends what's already committed (prefix match) and the capture
 * requirement is satisfied, only the new tail is written — no reload, no flicker.
 * Otherwise the document is reopened and fully rewritten.
 */
function display(content: string, needCapture: boolean): void {
	const c = committed;
	const canExtend =
		c !== null &&
		content.length >= c.content.length &&
		content.startsWith(c.content) &&
		(!needCapture || c.hasCapture);

	if (canExtend) {
		writeDoc(content.slice(c!.content.length));
		committed = { content, hasCapture: c!.hasCapture };
		return;
	}

	openDocument(needCapture);
	writeDoc(content || "<!-- empty -->");
	committed = { content, hasCapture: needCapture };
}

// --- Public API -----------------------------------------------------------

/** Render the current file fully (with console capture). */
export function render(): void {
	display(getFile(), true);
}

/**
 * Render a partial (in-progress) version of the file during streaming.
 * No console capture — keeps streaming smooth. Captured on the next full render.
 */
export function renderPartial(html: string): void {
	display(html, false);
}

/** Reset the committed state so the next display() reopens the document. */
export function invalidate(): void {
	committed = null;
}

/** Capture the iframe content as a base64 image. */
export async function getScreenshot(): Promise<string> {
	try {
		const iframeDoc = iframe.contentDocument;
		if (!iframeDoc || !iframe.contentWindow) {
			return "Unable to access iframe document.";
		}

		const width = iframe.clientWidth;
		const height = iframeDoc.body?.scrollHeight || iframe.clientHeight;

		const bodyHTML = iframeDoc.body?.innerHTML ?? "";
		const bodyStyle = iframeDoc.body?.style?.cssText ?? "";
		const computed = iframeDoc.defaultView?.getComputedStyle(iframeDoc.body ?? iframeDoc.documentElement) ?? null;
		const bgColor = computed?.backgroundColor ?? "#ffffff";

		const svg = `<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="${width}" height="${height}">
<foreignObject width="100%" height="100%">
<div xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" style="background-color: ${bgColor}; width: ${width}px; min-height: ${height}px; ${bodyStyle}">
${bodyHTML}
</div>
</foreignObject>
</svg>`;

		return btoa(unescape(encodeURIComponent(svg)));
	} catch (e) {
		return `Screenshot failed: ${(e as Error).message}`;
	}
}

/** Return captured console output. */
export function getConsole(): string {
	return consoleMessages.join("\n") || "(console is empty)";
}

/** Clear console messages. */
export function clearConsole(): void {
	consoleMessages.length = 0;
}

/** Force-reload the preview with a full render. */
export function reload(): void {
	clearConsole();
	render();
}

// --- Initialization -------------------------------------------------------

export function initPreview(): void {
	onChange(() => render());
	reloadBtn.addEventListener("click", () => reload());
	render();
}

# Sesión 5 — Demos

Las tres demos de la slide *Demo* del deck (`../deck/index.html`). Vienen de la charla de BeerJS *Pi: el agente que se construye solo* (2026-06-25). Van de la más chica a la más grande.

## 1 · Una mascota (`demo-1-mascot/`)

No hay código: la demo es pedirle a Pi, en vivo, que se escriba la extensión. `PROMPT.md` tiene el pedido: una mascota ASCII que camina debajo del input y festeja cuando corrés un comando con `!`, en un solo archivo TypeScript y sin dependencias.

- Correr Pi en un directorio vacío y pegarle el prompt.
- Probar con `/reload`, sin reiniciar.
- Lo que muestra: extender el harness es barato y el resultado se lee.

## 2 · Subagentes (`demo-2-subagents/`)

Una extensión de proyecto en `.pi/extensions/subagents.ts` con dos tools:

- **`delegate`** abre una sesión de Pi headless con su propio contexto, devuelve el control enseguida y, cuando termina, inyecta el resultado como `followUp`. Un widget muestra los subagentes activos.
- **`pipeline`** corre una lista de agentes en secuencia; cada uno recibe la salida del anterior (por ejemplo research → implement → review).

La sesión hija carga la misma extensión; la variable `PI_SUBAGENT_CHILD` evita que delegue de nuevo. Para correrla: `cd demo-2-subagents && pi` (Pi carga las extensiones de `.pi/extensions/` del proyecto).

## 3 · Pi en el navegador (`demo-3-browser-agent/`)

`pi-ai` y `pi-agent-core` corriendo en el navegador, sin backend: un chat a la izquierda y, a la derecha, la página que escribe el agente en un filesystem en memoria, renderizada en vivo. `PLAN.md` tiene el diseño completo.

```
cd demo-3-browser-agent
npm install
npm run dev
```

El modelo (`proveedor/modelo`, por defecto `zai/glm-5.2`) y la API key se cargan desde el engranaje de la app y quedan en el `localStorage` del navegador. El pedido de la charla: *"armame una landing page para una cafetería"*.

Las versiones de los paquetes (`@earendil-works/pi-ai` y `pi-agent-core` 0.79) son las de la charla; con Pi 1 puede hacer falta actualizarlas.

# Sesión 5 — Demos

Las tres demos de la slide *Demo* del deck (`../deck/index.html`). Vienen de la charla de BeerJS *Pi: el agente que se construye solo* (2026-06-25). Van de la más chica a la más grande.

## 1 · Una mascota (`demo-1-mascot/`)

No hay código: la demo es pedirle a Pi, en vivo, que se escriba la extensión. `PROMPT.md` tiene el pedido: una mascota ASCII que camina debajo del input y festeja cuando corrés un comando con `!`, en un solo archivo TypeScript y sin dependencias.

- Correr Pi en un directorio vacío y pegarle el prompt.
- Probar con `/reload`, sin reiniciar.
- Lo que muestra: extender el harness es barato y el resultado se lee.

## 2 · Subagentes (`demo-2-subagents/`)

Una extensión de proyecto en `.pi/extensions/subagents.ts` con dos tools:

- **`delegate`** abre una sesión de Pi headless con su propio contexto, devuelve el control enseguida y, cuando termina, inyecta el resultado como `followUp`. Un widget muestra los subagentes activos.
- **`pipeline`** corre una lista de agentes en secuencia; cada uno recibe la salida del anterior (por ejemplo research → implement → review).

La sesión hija carga la misma extensión; la variable `PI_SUBAGENT_CHILD` evita que delegue de nuevo. Para correrla: `cd demo-2-subagents && pi` (Pi carga las extensiones de `.pi/extensions/` del proyecto).

## 3 · Pi en el navegador (`demo-3-browser-agent/`)

`pi-ai` y `pi-agent-core` corriendo en el navegador, sin backend: un chat a la izquierda y, a la derecha, la página que escribe el agente en un filesystem en memoria, renderizada en vivo. `PLAN.md` tiene el diseño completo.

```
cd demo-3-browser-agent
npm install
npm run dev
```

El modelo (`proveedor/modelo`, por defecto `zai/glm-5.2`) y la API key se cargan desde el engranaje de la app y quedan en el `localStorage` del navegador. El pedido de la charla: *"armame una landing page para una cafetería"*.

Las versiones de los paquetes (`@earendil-works/pi-ai` y `pi-agent-core` 0.79) son las de la charla; con Pi 1 puede hacer falta actualizarlas.

**Tech stack**: Vite + TypeScript, vanilla DOM (no framework), `@earendil-works/pi-agent-core/base` + `@earendil-works/pi-ai/base`.

**LLM**: Configurable at runtime via a settings screen. User enters a `provider/model` string (e.g. `zai/glm-5.2`) and an API key. Common provider APIs (openai-completions, anthropic-messages, etc.) are registered at startup so any model works. Settings persist in `localStorage`.

### Key components

1. **Single in-memory file** — a string holding the entire HTML document (inline CSS in `<style>`, inline JS in `<script>`). No virtual filesystem, no paths — just one file.

2. **Custom browser tools** (five total):
   - `read()` — return the current HTML content of the single file
   - `write(content)` — replace the entire HTML content; triggers a preview re-render
   - `get_screenshot()` — capture the rendered iframe as a base64 image, return to the agent so it can visually verify its work
   - `get_console()` — return captured `console.log`/error output from the iframe
   - `reload()` — force-reload the iframe preview

3. **Agent** — `Agent` from `@earendil-works/pi-agent-core/base`, configured with:
   - Custom system prompt instructing it to build a single self-contained HTML page
   - The five browser tools
   - `getApiKey` callback that reads the key from settings
   - Model: resolved from the settings `provider/model` string via `getModel(provider, model)`

4. **LLM provider** — common provider APIs registered at startup (`openai-completions`, `anthropic-messages`). Calls go directly to the provider endpoint via native `fetch`. No backend proxy.

5. **Preview renderer** — when the single file changes, sets `iframe.srcdoc` to the new content. Injects a console-capture script that posts `console.log` and errors back to the parent via `postMessage`.

6. **Settings screen** — a gear icon in the chat panel header opens a modal with a text field for `provider/model` (e.g. `zai/glm-5.2`), a password field for the API key, and a save button. Values stored in `localStorage`.

7. **Chat UI** — subscribes to agent events, renders streaming text deltas, tool call indicators, and user messages. Input box pinned at the bottom; message history scrolls above it.

# Demo 3 — Pi in the browser

## Context

This is the closer for the "Pi, the self-building agent" talk (~5 min). The entire Pi agent loop runs **client-side in the browser** — no backend, no server. The audience sees a chat panel where they talk to the agent, and a live preview panel where the single HTML page the agent writes renders in real time.

**The wow moment**: Ask "build me a landing page for a coffee shop" and watch the agent write HTML on the left while the page assembles itself on the right.

## Architecture

```
┌─────────────────────┬──────────────────────────┐
│ Chat  [⚙ settings]  │   Live preview           │
│─────────────────────│   (right)                │
│   (left)            │                          │
│                     │   <iframe srcdoc="...">  │
│   Message history   │   (re-renders when       │
│   (scrollable)      │    the file changes)     │
│                     │                          │
│   Streaming text    │                          │
│   Tool call feed    │                          │
│   ("write…")       │                          │
│─────────────────────│                          │
│   [ input box...  ] │                          │
└─────────────────────┴──────────────────────────┘
```

**Tech stack**: Vite + TypeScript, vanilla DOM (no framework), `@earendil-works/pi-agent-core/base` + `@earendil-works/pi-ai/base`.

**LLM**: Configurable at runtime via a settings screen. User enters a `provider/model` string (e.g. `zai/glm-5.2`) and an API key. Common provider APIs (openai-completions, anthropic-messages, etc.) are registered at startup so any model works. Settings persist in `localStorage`.

### Key components

1. **Single in-memory file** — a string holding the entire HTML document (inline CSS in `<style>`, inline JS in `<script>`). No virtual filesystem, no paths — just one file.

2. **Custom browser tools** (five total):
   - `read()` — return the current HTML content of the single file
   - `write(content)` — replace the entire HTML content; triggers a preview re-render
   - `get_screenshot()` — capture the rendered iframe as a base64 image, return to the agent so it can visually verify its work
   - `get_console()` — return captured `console.log`/error output from the iframe
   - `reload()` — force-reload the iframe preview

3. **Agent** — `Agent` from `@earendil-works/pi-agent-core/base`, configured with:
   - Custom system prompt instructing it to build a single self-contained HTML page
   - The five browser tools
   - `getApiKey` callback that reads the key from settings
   - Model: resolved from the settings `provider/model` string via `getModel(provider, model)`

4. **LLM provider** — common provider APIs registered at startup (`openai-completions`, `anthropic-messages`). Calls go directly to the provider endpoint via native `fetch`. No backend proxy.

5. **Preview renderer** — when the single file changes, sets `iframe.srcdoc` to the new content. Injects a console-capture script that posts `console.log` and errors back to the parent via `postMessage`.

6. **Settings screen** — a gear icon in the chat panel header opens a modal with a text field for `provider/model` (e.g. `zai/glm-5.2`), a password field for the API key, and a save button. Values stored in `localStorage`.

7. **Chat UI** — subscribes to agent events, renders streaming text deltas, tool call indicators, and user messages. Input box pinned at the bottom; message history scrolls above it.

## Files to create

```
demo-3-browser-agent/
├── index.html              # Entry HTML with two-panel layout + settings modal
├── package.json            # Vite + TS + pi packages
├── tsconfig.json
├── vite.config.ts          # Vite config
├── src/
│   ├── main.ts             # App entry: wire agent → UI
│   ├── file.ts             # Single in-memory file + change notifications
│   ├── browser-tools.ts    # read / write / get_screenshot / get_console / reload
│   ├── agent.ts            # Agent setup (system prompt, model, tools, events)
│   ├── preview.ts          # Renders the single file into the iframe + console capture
│   ├── settings.ts         # Settings modal: provider/model + API key (localStorage)
│   ├── chat-ui.ts          # Chat panel: message list, input box, tool feed
│   └── style.css           # Two-panel layout + chat styling
└── PLAN.md
```

## Reuse

- `Agent` class and `AgentTool` interface from `@earendil-works/pi-agent-core/base`
- `getModel`, `Type` (typebox) from `@earendil-works/pi-ai/base`
- Provider `register()` from `@earendil-works/pi-ai/openai-completions` (and `anthropic-messages` if needed)
- `streamSimple` is used internally by `Agent` as the default `streamFn` — no need to import it explicitly
- The base README documents this exact browser pattern: `import { Agent } from "@earendil-works/pi-agent-core/base"; import { getModel } from "@earendil-works/pi-ai/base"; register();`
- `getModel(provider, model)` parses the `provider/model` settings string

## System prompt (draft)

```
You are a web developer running entirely in the browser.
You have tools to write, read, and verify a single self-contained HTML page.

- write(content): Replace the entire HTML page. Inline all CSS in <style> and all JS in <script>.
- read(): Read the current HTML content.
- get_screenshot(): Capture the rendered page to visually verify your work.
- get_console(): Read browser console output and errors.
- reload(): Force-reload the preview.

The preview panel renders your HTML in real time.
Be concise in your explanations — let the code speak.
```

## Steps

- [ ] Scaffold Vite + TypeScript project
- [ ] Install `@earendil-works/pi-agent-core@^0.79.9` and `@earendil-works/pi-ai@^0.79.9`
- [ ] Verify Z.AI GLM-5.2 bundles cleanly for the browser (OpenAI SDK + `openai-completions` provider)
- [ ] Implement single-file store (string + callback-based change notifications)
- [ ] Implement browser tools: `read`, `write`, `get_screenshot`, `get_console`, `reload`
- [ ] Implement settings modal (`provider/model` text field + API key password field, persisted in localStorage)
- [ ] Register common provider APIs at startup (openai-completions, anthropic-messages)
- [ ] Implement agent setup (system prompt, model from settings, tools, `getApiKey`)
- [ ] Build two-panel HTML layout + CSS
- [ ] Build chat UI (agent event subscription → DOM updates)
- [ ] Build preview renderer (single file → iframe srcdoc + console capture injection)
- [ ] Build settings UI (modal, gear icon, localStorage)
- [ ] Wire everything together in `main.ts`
- [ ] Test end-to-end: "build a landing page for a coffee shop"
- [ ] Verify provider SDK bundles cleanly for the browser (OpenAI SDK for openai-completions)
- [ ] Git init + initial commit

## Verification

1. `npm install && npm run dev` — Vite dev server starts
2. Click the settings gear, enter model (e.g. `zai/glm-5.2`) and API key, save
3. Type "build me a landing page for a coffee shop"
4. Watch: agent streams text on the left, tool calls appear ("write…"), and the page assembles on the right in real time
5. The preview should show a rendered self-contained HTML page
6. Agent can call `get_screenshot` to visually verify its work and `get_console` to debug
7. If CORS blocks direct browser→provider calls, add a Vite dev proxy as a fallback (dev only, not needed for the talk's point about client-side execution)

# Demo 3 — Pi in the browser

## Context

This is the closer for the "Pi, the self-building agent" talk (~5 min). The entire Pi agent loop runs **client-side in the browser** — no backend, no server. The audience sees a chat panel where they talk to the agent, and a live preview panel where the single HTML page the agent writes renders in real time.

**The wow moment**: Ask "build me a landing page for a coffee shop" and watch the agent write HTML on the left while the page assembles itself on the right.

## Architecture

```
┌─────────────────────┬──────────────────────────┐
│ Chat  [⚙ settings]  │   Live preview           │
│─────────────────────│   (right)                │
│   (left)            │                          │
│                     │   <iframe srcdoc="...">  │
│   Message history   │   (re-renders when       │
│   (scrollable)      │    the file changes)     │
│                     │                          │
│   Streaming text    │                          │
│   Tool call feed    │                          │
│   ("write…")       │                          │
│─────────────────────│                          │
│   [ input box...  ] │                          │
└─────────────────────┴──────────────────────────┘
```

**Tech stack**: Vite + TypeScript, vanilla DOM (no framework), `@earendil-works/pi-agent-core` + `@earendil-works/pi-ai` + `@earendil-works/pi-schema` (tool parameters).

**LLM**: Configurable at runtime via a settings screen. User enters a `provider/model` string (e.g. `zai/glm-5.2`) and an API key. Every built-in provider is registered at startup (`builtinModels()`) so any model in the catalog works. Settings persist in `localStorage`.

### Key components

1. **Single in-memory file** — a string holding the entire HTML document (inline CSS in `<style>`, inline JS in `<script>`). No virtual filesystem, no paths — just one file.

2. **Custom browser tools** (five total):
   - `read()` — return the current HTML content of the single file
   - `write(content)` — replace the entire HTML content; triggers a preview re-render
   - `get_screenshot()` — capture the rendered iframe as a base64 image, return to the agent so it can visually verify its work
   - `get_console()` — return captured `console.log`/error output from the iframe
   - `reload()` — force-reload the iframe preview

3. **Agent** — `Agent` from `@earendil-works/pi-agent-core`, configured with:
   - Custom system prompt instructing it to build a single self-contained HTML page
   - The five browser tools
   - `streamFn: models.streamSimple.bind(models)`
   - `getApiKey` callback that reads the key from settings (browsers have no env vars, so the key is passed explicitly)
   - Model: resolved from the settings `provider/model` string via `models.getModel(provider, model)`

4. **LLM provider** — a `Models` collection from `builtinModels()` (`@earendil-works/pi-ai/providers/all`); provider SDKs load lazily on the first request. Calls go directly to the provider endpoint via native `fetch`. No backend proxy.

5. **Preview renderer** — when the single file changes, sets `iframe.srcdoc` to the new content. Injects a console-capture script that posts `console.log` and errors back to the parent via `postMessage`.

6. **Settings screen** — a gear icon in the chat panel header opens a modal with a text field for `provider/model` (e.g. `zai/glm-5.2`), a password field for the API key, and a save button. Values stored in `localStorage`.

7. **Chat UI** — subscribes to agent events, renders streaming text deltas, tool call indicators, and user messages. Input box pinned at the bottom; message history scrolls above it.

import {
	createAgentSession,
	DefaultResourceLoader,
	getAgentDir,
	SessionManager,
	SettingsManager,
	type ExtensionAPI,
	type ExtensionContext,
} from "@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent";
import { Text } from "@earendil-works/pi-tui";
import { Type } from "typebox";

// The child SDK session loads this same extension, so this flag prevents recursive delegation.
const SUBAGENT_ENV = "PI_SUBAGENT_CHILD";
const SUBAGENT_RESULT_TYPE = "subagent-result";
const ACTIVE_SUBAGENTS_WIDGET = "active-subagents";
const DEFAULT_SUBAGENT_TOOLS = ["read", "grep", "find", "ls"];

interface BackgroundTask {
	id: string;
	label: string;
	task: string;
	status: "running" | "done" | "failed";
	output?: string;
	error?: string;
}

interface SubagentOptions {
	systemPrompt: string;
	tools: string[];
}

interface PipelineAgent {
	name: string;
	instructions: string;
	tools?: string[];
}

// Pull the final assistant text out of the child session after it finishes.
const getFinalText = (session: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof createAgentSession>>["session"]): string => {
	for (let i = session.messages.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
		const message = session.messages[i];
		if (message.role !== "assistant") continue;

		for (const part of message.content) {
			if (part.type === "text") return part.text;
		}
	}

	return "Subagent finished without text output.";
};

const defaultSubagentOptions: SubagentOptions = {
	systemPrompt: [
		"You are a focused subagent running inside an isolated Pi agent session.",
		"Use the available read-only tools to inspect the project when useful.",
		"Return a concise report for the parent agent.",
	].join("\n"),
	tools: DEFAULT_SUBAGENT_TOOLS,
};

// Create a fresh in-memory Pi agent session and run the delegated task inside it.
const runSubagent = async (
	ctx: Pick<ExtensionContext, "cwd" | "model" | "modelRegistry">,
	task: string,
	options = defaultSubagentOptions,
): Promise<string> => {
	// Keep normal resource loading, but replace the system prompt for the child.
	const loader = new DefaultResourceLoader({
		cwd: ctx.cwd,
		agentDir: getAgentDir(),
		systemPromptOverride: () => options.systemPrompt,
		appendSystemPromptOverride: () => [],
	});

	// Mark resource loading as child-only so this extension opts out.
	process.env[SUBAGENT_ENV] = "1";
	try {
		await loader.reload();
	} finally {
		delete process.env[SUBAGENT_ENV];
	}

	// The subagent has its own context window, session state, tools, and model loop.
	const { session } = await createAgentSession({
		cwd: ctx.cwd,
		model: ctx.model,
		modelRegistry: ctx.modelRegistry,
		resourceLoader: loader,
		sessionManager: SessionManager.inMemory(ctx.cwd),
		settingsManager: SettingsManager.inMemory(),
		tools: options.tools,
	});

	try {
		await session.prompt(task);
		return getFinalText(session);
	} finally {
		session.dispose();
	}
};

const runPipeline = async (
	ctx: Pick<ExtensionContext, "cwd" | "model" | "modelRegistry">,
	task: string,
	agents: PipelineAgent[],
): Promise<string> => {
	let previousOutput = "";
	const outputs: string[] = [];

	for (const [index, agent] of agents.entries()) {
		const output = await runSubagent(
			ctx,
			[
				`Overall task:\n${task}`,
				previousOutput ? `Previous step output:\n${previousOutput}` : "This is the first pipeline step.",
				"Complete your assigned step and return a concise handoff for the next agent.",
			].join("\n\n"),
			{
				systemPrompt: agent.instructions,
				tools: agent.tools?.length ? agent.tools : DEFAULT_SUBAGENT_TOOLS,
			},
		);

		outputs.push(`## ${index + 1}. ${agent.name}\n\n${output}`);
		previousOutput = output;
	}

	return outputs.join("\n\n");
};

export default function subagents(pi: ExtensionAPI) {
	// Child sessions load normal project extensions, but should not get their own delegate tool.
	if (process.env[SUBAGENT_ENV] === "1") return;

	let nextTaskNumber = 1;
	const tasks = new Map<string, BackgroundTask>();

	const updateActiveSubagents = (ctx: ExtensionContext) => {
		if (!ctx.hasUI) return;

		const activeTasks = Array.from(tasks.values()).filter((task) => task.status === "running");
		if (activeTasks.length === 0) {
			ctx.ui.setWidget(ACTIVE_SUBAGENTS_WIDGET, undefined);
			return;
		}

		ctx.ui.setWidget(ACTIVE_SUBAGENTS_WIDGET, [
			`Active subagents: ${activeTasks.length}`,
			...activeTasks.map((task) => `⏳ ${task.id} (${task.label}) — ${task.task}`),
		]);
	};

	const startBackgroundTask = (ctx: ExtensionContext, label: string, requestedTask: string, run: () => Promise<string>) => {
		const id = `${label}-${nextTaskNumber++}`;
		const task: BackgroundTask = { id, label, task: requestedTask, status: "running" };
		tasks.set(id, task);
		updateActiveSubagents(ctx);

		run()
			.then((output) => {
				task.status = "done";
				task.output = output;
				updateActiveSubagents(ctx);

				pi.sendMessage(
					{
						customType: SUBAGENT_RESULT_TYPE,
						content: `Task ${id} finished.\n\n${output}`,
						display: true,
						details: { id, task: requestedTask, output },
					},
					{ deliverAs: "followUp", triggerTurn: true },
				);
			})
			.catch((error: unknown) => {
				task.status = "failed";
				task.error = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
				updateActiveSubagents(ctx);

				pi.sendMessage(
					{
						customType: SUBAGENT_RESULT_TYPE,
						content: `Task ${id} failed.\n\n${task.error}`,
						display: true,
						details: { id, task: requestedTask, error: task.error },
					},
					{ deliverAs: "followUp", triggerTurn: true },
				);
			});

		return task;
	};

	pi.registerMessageRenderer(SUBAGENT_RESULT_TYPE, (message, _options, theme) => {
		return new Text(theme.fg("success", "✓ subagent result") + "\n" + message.content, 0, 0);
	});

	pi.registerTool({
		name: "delegate",
		label: "Delegate",
		description: "Start one focused background subagent task and return a task handle immediately.",
		parameters: Type.Object({
			task: Type.String({ description: "The focused task to hand to the subagent" }),
		}),
		promptSnippet: "Start focused research or inspection tasks in isolated background subagents.",
		promptGuidelines: ["Use delegate when a focused independent task can run in the background while you continue working."],

		async execute(_toolCallId, params, _signal, _onUpdate, ctx) {
			// Background mode: return a handle now, then inject the child result later.
			const task = startBackgroundTask(ctx, "subagent", params.task, () => runSubagent(ctx, params.task));

			return {
				content: [{ type: "text", text: `Started ${task.id}. I can keep working while it runs.` }],
				details: { id: task.id, task: params.task, status: task.status },
			};
		},

		renderCall(args, theme) {
			return new Text(
				theme.fg("toolTitle", theme.bold("delegate ")) + theme.fg("dim", args.task ?? ""),
				0,
				0,
			);
		},

		renderResult(result, _options, theme) {
			const text = result.content.find((part) => part.type === "text")?.text ?? "";
			return new Text(theme.fg("warning", "⏳ subagent started") + "\n" + text, 0, 0);
		},
	});

	pi.registerTool({
		name: "pipeline",
		label: "Pipeline",
		description: "Start a configurable background pipeline of subagents that run in sequence.",
		parameters: Type.Object({
			task: Type.String({ description: "The overall task for the pipeline" }),
			agents: Type.Array(
				Type.Object({
					name: Type.String({ description: "Short label for this pipeline agent" }),
					instructions: Type.String({ description: "System instructions for this pipeline agent" }),
					tools: Type.Optional(
						Type.Array(Type.String({ description: "Tool name available to this agent" }), {
							description: "Optional tool allowlist. Defaults to read, grep, find, and ls.",
						}),
					),
				}),
				{ minItems: 1, description: "Agents to run in order" },
			),
		}),
		promptSnippet: "Run a configurable background pipeline of subagents in sequence.",
		promptGuidelines: ["Use pipeline when the user asks for a custom multi-agent workflow with ordered steps."],

		async execute(_toolCallId, params, _signal, _onUpdate, ctx) {
			const task = startBackgroundTask(ctx, "pipeline", params.task, () => runPipeline(ctx, params.task, params.agents));

			return {
				content: [
					{ type: "text", text: `Started ${task.id}. ${params.agents.length} agents will run in sequence.` },
				],
				details: { id: task.id, task: params.task, agents: params.agents, status: task.status },
			};
		},

		renderCall(args, theme) {
			return new Text(
				theme.fg("toolTitle", theme.bold("pipeline ")) +
					theme.fg("dim", `${args.agents?.length ?? 0} agents — ${args.task ?? ""}`),
				0,
				0,
			);
		},

		renderResult(result, _options, theme) {
			const text = result.content.find((part) => part.type === "text")?.text ?? "";
			return new Text(theme.fg("warning", "⏳ pipeline started") + "\n" + text, 0, 0);
		},
	});
}
</result>

				theme.fg("toolTitle", theme.bold("delegate ")) + theme.fg("dim", args.task ?? ""),
				0,
				0,
			);
		},

			const text = result.content.find((part) => part.type === "text")?.text ?? "";
			return new Text(theme.fg("warning", "⏳ subagent started") + "\n" + text, 0, 0);
		},
	});

		name: "pipeline",
		label: "Pipeline",
		description: "Start a configurable background pipeline of subagents that run in sequence.",
		parameters: Type.Object({
			task: Type.String({ description: "The overall task for the pipeline" }),
			agents: Type.Array(
				Type.Object({
					name: Type.String({ description: "Short label for this pipeline agent" }),
					instructions: Type.String({ description: "System instructions for this pipeline agent" }),
					tools: Type.Optional(
						Type.Array(Type.String({ description: "Tool name available to this agent" }), {
							description: "Optional tool allowlist. Defaults to read, grep, find, and ls.",
						}),
					),
				}),
				{ minItems: 1, description: "Agents to run in order" },
			),
		}),
		promptSnippet: "Run a configurable background pipeline of subagents in sequence.",
		promptGuidelines: ["Use pipeline when the user asks for a custom multi-agent workflow with ordered steps."],

		async execute(_toolCallId, params, _signal, _onUpdate, ctx) {
			const task = startBackgroundTask(ctx, "pipeline", params.task, () => runPipeline(ctx, params.task, params.agents));

			return {
				content: [
					{ type: "text", text: `Started ${task.id}. ${params.agents.length} agents will run in sequence.` },
				],
				details: { id: task.id, task: params.task, agents: params.agents, status: task.status },
			};
		},

		renderCall(args, theme) {
			return new Text(
				theme.fg("toolTitle", theme.bold("pipeline ")) +
					theme.fg("dim", `${args.agents?.length ?? 0} agents — ${args.task ?? ""}`),
				0,
				0,
			);
		},

		renderResult(result, _options, theme) {
			const text = result.content.find((part) => part.type === "text")?.text ?? "";

		},

Returning `systemPrompt`, or setting `forceSystemPrompt`, replaces the whole prompt for the run: every provider receives the forced text as its leading system prompt (a cache miss when it changes), and the session transcript keeps recording the structured sections. Tool selection changes update both the prompt contributions and executable provider tools; calling `pi.setActiveTools()` inside the handler has the same effect as editing `selectedTools`. 	/** Global config directory. Default: ~/.pi/agent */

	/** Model to use. Default: from settings, else first available */
	model?: Model<any>;
	/** Thinking level. Default: from settings, else 'medium' (clamped to model capabilities) */
	thinkingLevel?: ThinkingLevel;
	/** Models available for cycling (Ctrl+P in interactive mode) */
	scopedModels?: Array<{ model: Model<any>; thinkingLevel?: ThinkingLevel }>;

	/**

	 *
	 * - "all": start with no tools enabled
	 * - "builtin": disable the default built-in tools (read, bash, edit, write)
	 *   but keep extension/custom tools enabled

	noTools?: "all" | "builtin";
	/**
	 * Optional allowlist of tool names or patterns, where `*` matches any characters.
	 *
	 * When omitted, pi uses the resolved `defaultTools` setting for the initial
	 * selection when configured. Otherwise it enables the default built-in tools
	 * (read, bash, edit, write). Extension/custom tools remain enabled unless
	 * `noTools` changes that default. When provided, only matching tools are

	 * These entries take exact names. Mixing them with plain entries throws.

	tools?: string[];
	/**

	excludeTools?: string[];

	customTools?: ToolDefinition[];

	resourceLoader?: ResourceLoader;

	/** Session manager. Default: SessionManager.create(cwd) */
	sessionManager?: SessionManager;

	/** Settings manager. Default: SettingsManager.create(cwd, agentDir) */
	settingsManager?: SettingsManager;
	/** Session start event metadata for extension runtime startup. */
	sessionStartEvent?: SessionStartEvent;

	if (toolListError) throw new Error(`Invalid tools option: ${toolListError}`);
	const defaultToolNames = options.noTools ? [] : (settingsManager.getDefaultTools() ?? DEFAULT_TOOL_NAMES);
	// A `tools` list of only `+name`/`-name` entries changes the default selection instead of
	// replacing it, like the `defaultTools` setting.
	const toolModifiers = options.tools?.some(isToolModifier) ? options.tools : undefined;
	const selectedToolNames = toolModifiers ? applyToolModifiers(defaultToolNames, toolModifiers) : options.tools;
	const allowedToolNames = toolModifiers
		? options.noTools === "all"
			? selectedToolNames
			: undefined
		: (options.tools ?? (options.noTools === "all" ? [] : undefined));
	const excludedToolNames = options.excludeTools;
	const isExcludedTool = excludedToolNames ? createToolNameMatcher(excludedToolNames) : undefined;
	const initialActiveToolNames = (selectedToolNames ?? defaultToolNames).filter((name) => !isExcludedTool?.(name));

	// Create convertToLlm wrapper that filters images if blockImages is enabled (defense-in-depth)
	const convertToLlmWithBlockImages = (messages: AgentMessage[]): Message[] => {
		const converted = convertToLlm(messages);
		// Check setting dynamically so mid-session changes take effect
		if (!settingsManager.getBlockImages()) {
			return converted;
		}
		// Filter out ImageContent from all messages, replacing with text placeholder
		return converted.map((msg) => {
			if (msg.role === "user" || msg.role === "toolResult") {
				const content = msg.content;
				if (Array.isArray(content)) {
					const hasImages = content.some((c) => c.type === "image");
					if (hasImages) {
						const filteredContent = content
							.map((c) =>
								c.type === "image" ? { type: "text" as const, text: "Image reading is disabled." } : c,
							)
							.filter(
								(c, i, arr) =>
									// Dedupe consecutive "Image reading is disabled." texts
									!(
										c.type === "text" &&
										c.text === "Image reading is disabled." &&
										i > 0 &&
										arr[i - 1].type === "text" &&
										(arr[i - 1] as { type: "text"; text: string }).text === "Image reading is disabled."
									),
							);
						return { ...msg, content: filteredContent };
					}
				}
			}
			return msg;
		});
	};

	const extensionRunnerRef: { current?: ExtensionRunner } = {};
	const cacheWarmer = new CacheWarmer(
		modelRuntime,
		sessionManager,
		() => settingsManager.getCacheWarmingMode(),
		async (event) => extensionRunnerRef.current?.emitCacheWarmingDecision(event) ?? event.action,
	);
	const buildRequestOptions = (options: ModelsSimpleStreamOptions = {}): ModelsSimpleStreamOptions => {
		const providerRetrySettings = settingsManager.getProviderRetrySettings();
		const httpIdleTimeoutMs = settingsManager.getHttpIdleTimeoutMs();
		const effectiveTimeoutMs = httpIdleTimeoutMs === 0 ? 2147483647 : httpIdleTimeoutMs;
		const headerRunner = extensionRunnerRef.current;
		return {
			...options,
			timeoutMs: options.timeoutMs ?? providerRetrySettings.timeoutMs ?? effectiveTimeoutMs,
			websocketConnectTimeoutMs: options.websocketConnectTimeoutMs ?? settingsManager.getWebSocketConnectTimeoutMs(),
			maxRetries: options.maxRetries ?? providerRetrySettings.maxRetries,
			maxRetryDelayMs: options.maxRetryDelayMs ?? providerRetrySettings.maxRetryDelayMs,
			// Replaces the agent loop's default identity; read per request so telemetry changes apply at once.
			identity: getClientIdentity(settingsManager),
			transformHeaders: async (headers) =>
				headerRunner?.hasHandlers("before_provider_headers")
					? headerRunner.emitBeforeProviderHeaders(headers)
					: headers,
		};
	};
	// Warm only requests for the selected model. Requests a virtual selection routed, or that an
	// extension redirected, may not be repeated by the next request, so warming them could be wasted.
	const cacheContextIsCurrent = (requestModel: Model<any>) => {
		const messages = agent.state.messages;
		return () => {
			const currentModel = agent.state.model;
			const currentMessages = agent.state.messages;
			return (
				currentModel.provider === requestModel.provider &&
				currentModel.id === requestModel.id &&
				messages.length <= currentMessages.length &&
				messages.every((message, index) => currentMessages[index] === message)
			);
		};
	};
	const transformProviderPayload = async (payload: unknown) => {
		const runner = extensionRunnerRef.current;
		if (!runner?.hasHandlers("before_provider_request")) return payload;
		return runner.emitBeforeProviderRequest(payload);
	};
	const handleProviderResponse: NonNullable<ModelsSimpleStreamOptions["onResponse"]> = async (response) => {
		const runner = extensionRunnerRef.current;
		if (!runner?.hasHandlers("after_provider_response")) return;
		await runner.emit({
			type: "after_provider_response",
			status: response.status,
			headers: response.headers,
		});
	};
	const handleProviderStreamEvent: NonNullable<ModelsSimpleStreamOptions["onProviderStreamEvent"]> = async (
		data,
		model,
	) => {
		const runner = extensionRunnerRef.current;
		if (!runner?.hasHandlers("provider_stream_event")) return;
		await runner.emit({
			data,
			type: "provider_stream_event",
			provider: model.provider,
			api: model.api,
			model: model.id,
		});
	};

	const agent = new Agent({
		initialState: {
			systemPrompt: "",
			model,
			thinkingLevel,
			tools: [],
			messages: existingSession.messages,
		},
		convertToLlm: convertToLlmWithBlockImages,
		streamFn: async (model, context, options) => {
			const requestOptions = buildRequestOptions(options);
			// Compaction and summaries use their own routing ids; only session requests
			// replace the cache entry, so warming restarts from them. Keep warming while
			// the current transcript still extends the request's prefix. Agent state may
			// shallow-copy the messages array or refresh the model object without changing
			// the provider request, so top-level object identity is not a valid cache key.
			if (options?.sessionId === sessionManager.getSessionId()) {
				cacheWarmer.start({ model, context, options: requestOptions }, cacheContextIsCurrent(model));
			}
			return modelRuntime.streamSimple(model, context, requestOptions);
		},
		onPayload: transformProviderPayload,
		onResponse: handleProviderResponse,
		onProviderStreamEvent: handleProviderStreamEvent,
		sessionId: sessionManager.getSessionId(),
		transformContext: async (messages) => {
			const runner = extensionRunnerRef.current;
			if (!runner) return messages;
			return runner.emitContext(messages);
		},
		steeringMode: settingsManager.getSteeringMode(),
		followUpMode: settingsManager.getFollowUpMode(),
		transport: settingsManager.getTransport(),
		thinkingBudgets: settingsManager.getThinkingBudgets(),
		maxRetryDelayMs: settingsManager.getProviderRetrySettings().maxRetryDelayMs,
	});
	// This stream resolves auth through modelRuntime, so summaries must not pre-resolve it (#11520).
	markRuntimeStreamFunction(agent.streamFunction, modelRuntime);

	// Restore missing settings metadata for older sessions.
	if (hasExistingSession) {
		if (!hasThinkingEntry) {
			sessionManager.appendThinkingLevelChange(thinkingLevel);
		}
	} else {
		// Save initial model and thinking level for new sessions so they can be restored on resume
		if (model) {
			sessionManager.appendModelChange(model.provider, model.id);
		}
		sessionManager.appendThinkingLevelChange(thinkingLevel);
	}

	const session = new AgentSession({
		agent,
		sessionManager,
		settingsManager,
		cwd,
		scopedModels: options.scopedModels,
		resourceLoader,
		customTools: options.customTools,
		modelRuntime,
		cacheWarmer,
		initialActiveToolNames,
		usesDefaultTools: (options.tools === undefined || toolModifiers !== undefined) && !options.noTools,
		defaultToolModifiers: toolModifiers,
		allowedToolNames,
		excludedToolNames,
		extensionRunnerRef,
		sessionStartEvent: options.sessionStartEvent,
	});

	const extensionsResult = resourceLoader.getExtensions();

	return {
		session,
		extensionsResult,
		modelFallbackMessage,
	};
}

sdk.md:98:Without overrides, the factory creates a `ModelRuntime`, file-backed `SettingsManager`, persistent `SessionManager`, `DefaultResourceLoader`, and the configured default tools.
sdk.md:102:- `modelRuntime`, `model`, `thinkingLevel`, and `scopedModels` control model access and selection.
extensions.md:1216:### ctx.modelRegistry / ctx.model / ctx.thinkingLevel / ctx.scopedModels
extensions.md:1218:Access to models, providers, and resolved authentication. `ctx.modelRegistry.getProvider(id)` returns the effective pi-ai provider, while `getProviderAuth(id)` resolves its current API key, headers, base URL, and provider-scoped environment without requiring a loaded model. `ctx.model` is the active model, and `ctx.thinkingLevel` is its current effective thinking level.
extensions.md:1220:`ctx.scopedModels` is the read-only list of models scoped to the current session — the same set the `/scoped-models` command shows. It is resolved at session start from the `--models` CLI flag and the `enabledModels` setting (matched against the available catalogue with minimatch on `provider/modelId` or a bare `modelId`). It is empty when no scoping is configured, meaning every available model is usable. Each entry is `{ model, thinkingLevel? }`, where `thinkingLevel` is set only when a pattern pinned it (e.g. `anthropic/*:high`). Use it to populate a model picker that mirrors the built-in one instead of enumerating the whole catalogue via `ctx.modelRegistry.getAvailable()`.
extensions.md:1224:Use `ctx.modelRegistry.streamSimple(model, context, options)` for provider-neutral options such as `reasoning`, or `complete(model, context, options)` to await the final assistant message with API-specific options. Both use configured providers and resolve authentication, including for providers registered with `pi.registerProvider()`. Use these instead of `pi-ai/compat` streaming functions, which cannot see extension provider registrations.
extensions.md:1945:const model = ctx.modelRegistry.find("anthropic", "claude-sonnet-4-5");
extensions.md:1982:`context.signal` is always a concrete signal and provider callbacks must pass it to blocking I/O. Public `ModelRuntime.refresh()` and `ModelRegistry.refresh()` calls accept an optional signal and are unbounded when it is omitted; extensions and applications choose their own deadlines. Cancellation stops the caller waiting even if a provider ignores the signal, but cooperation is still required to stop the underlying work.
670:- Added `models.generateImages()` to codemode scripts. It runs image models such as OpenRouter's with the session's credentials and returns base64 image blocks that `image()` attaches to the result; usage counts toward the session cost like `models.classify()`. Extensions can call `ctx.modelRegistry.generateImages()`. See [Use image models](docs/models.md#use-image-models).
781:- Added image generation to `ModelRuntime`: `generateImages()` with runtime-resolved auth (stored credentials, OAuth, runtime API keys, `models.json` headers), plus `getModelsOfType()`, `getModelOfType()`, `getAvailableOfType()`, `getAllModels()`, and `getAllAvailable()`. OpenRouter image models are listed under the `openrouter` provider and share its credential; an upstream ID can have separate chat and image entries. `models.json` providers and extension registrations without a model list keep built-in image generation. Extension model lists can include discriminated chat, image, and classifier entries with operation implementations; when supplied, they replace the provider catalog across every operation. Chat-facing reads (`getModels()`, `getAvailableSnapshot()`, the model picker) are unchanged.
782:- Added classifier support to `ModelRuntime`, including `classify()`, classifier model accessors, runtime-resolved authentication, and the built-in TypeSafe `jev-latest` model.
943:- Added `ctx.modelRegistry.stream()` and `streamSimple()` for extension model calls through configured providers with resolved authentication ([#8964](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/8964)).
1307:- `ModelRegistry.getApiKeyAndHeaders()` now returns `ProviderHeaders` with `string | null` values and preserves `null` header-deletion markers. Extensions that inspect returned headers must handle `null`; extensions forwarding them to pi-ai streams should pass them through unchanged. This prevents placeholder OpenAI credentials from being sent through Cloudflare AI Gateway ([#7030](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/7030)).
1308:- Changed `ModelRegistry.refresh()` to accept `ModelsRefreshOptions` and return `ModelsRefreshResult` instead of discarding cancellation and provider errors.
1309:- Changed `ModelRuntime.setRuntimeApiKey()` to accept auth cancellation options rather than catalog refresh options. Call `refresh({ providers: [providerId], signal })` separately when remote freshness is required.
1504:- Exposed the session's resolved model scope as `ctx.scopedModels` to extensions. See [Extension Context](docs/extensions.md#ctxmodelregistry--ctxmodel--ctxthinkinglevel--ctxscopedmodels) ([#7191](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/7191) by [@pungggi](https://github.com/pungggi), [#7215](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/7215)).
1703:- **Unified model runtime and provider authentication** — `ModelRuntime` centralizes model configuration, provider-owned `/login`, and dynamic provider catalogs. See [Providers](docs/providers.md).
1709:- Replaced the SDK's `CreateAgentSessionOptions.authStorage` and `modelRegistry` options with the async `modelRuntime` option. `AuthStorage` and its storage backends are no longer exported; use `ModelRuntime` (or a custom pi-ai `CredentialStore`), or `readStoredCredential()` for one-off reads of auth.json.
1710:- Removed redundant `ModelRuntime.getAll()`, `find()`, `getSnapshot()`, and `getAuthOptions()` projections. Use the pi-ai `Models` methods `getModels()`, `getModel()`, `getProviders()`, and `checkAuth()` directly.
1711:- Replaced SDK request-auth assembly through `ModelRegistry.getApiKeyAndHeaders()` with `ModelRuntime.getAuth()`. Passing a provider ID returns provider-scoped auth; passing a model also resolves built-in, `models.json`, and extension model headers.
1712:- Changed extension-facing `ModelRegistry.refresh()` from synchronous `void` to `Promise<void>` because `models.json` loading is asynchronous. Extensions must await it before making synchronous registry reads.
1713:- Moved canonical dynamic catalog refresh to async `ModelRuntime.refresh()`/pi-ai `Models.refresh()`. Legacy extension OAuth `modifyModels` remains supported as a synchronous compatibility projection after credential initialization.
1717:- Added `ModelRuntime` as the canonical async SDK and internal model/auth facade while preserving the synchronous extension-facing `ModelRegistry` API. `ModelRuntime.create()` accepts any pi-ai `CredentialStore` through its `credentials` option.
1726:- Changed `ModelRuntime` to compose built-in providers, immutable `models.json` configuration, and extension overlays through ad-hoc pi-ai provider methods.
1727:- Changed `ModelRuntime` to own final request assembly: `getAuth(model)` includes configured model headers, stream methods resolve auth once, and `before_provider_headers` runs as the Models-only header transform before provider dispatch.
3297:- `ModelRegistry` no longer has a public constructor. SDK callers and tests must use `ModelRegistry.create(authStorage, modelsJsonPath?)` for file-backed registries or `ModelRegistry.inMemory(authStorage)` for built-in-only registries. Direct `new ModelRegistry(...)` calls no longer compile.
3351:- `ModelRegistry.getApiKey(model)` has been replaced by `getApiKeyAndHeaders(model)` because `models.json` auth and header values can now resolve dynamically on every request. Extensions and SDK integrations that previously fetched only an API key must now fetch request auth per call and forward both `apiKey` and `headers`. Use `getApiKeyForProvider(provider)` only when you explicitly want provider-level API key lookup without model headers or `authHeader` handling ([#1835](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/issues/1835))

setDefaultStreamFn(streamSimple);

export interface CreateAgentSessionOptions {
	/** Working directory for project-local discovery. Default: process.cwd() */
	cwd?: string;
	/** Global config directory. Default: ~/.pi/agent */
	agentDir?: string;

	/** Canonical model/auth runtime. Defaults to a runtime using agentDir/auth.json and models.json. */
	modelRuntime?: ModelRuntime;

	/** Model to use. Default: from settings, else first available */
	model?: Model<any>;
	/** Thinking level. Default: from settings, else 'medium' (clamped to model capabilities) */
	thinkingLevel?: ThinkingLevel;
	/** Models available for cycling (Ctrl+P in interactive mode) */
	scopedModels?: Array<{ model: Model<any>; thinkingLevel?: ThinkingLevel }>;

	/**
	 * Optional default tool suppression mode when no explicit allowlist is provided.
	 *
	 * - "all": start with no tools enabled
	 * - "builtin": disable the default built-in tools (read, bash, edit, write)
	 *   but keep extension/custom tools enabled
	 */
	noTools?: "all" | "builtin";
	/**
	 * Optional allowlist of tool names or patterns, where `*` matches any characters.
	 *
	 * When omitted, pi uses the resolved `defaultTools` setting for the initial
	 * selection when configured. Otherwise it enables the default built-in tools
	 * (read, bash, edit, write). Extension/custom tools remain enabled unless
	 * `noTools` changes that default. When provided, only matching tools are
	 * enabled. MCP tools stay registered for codemode and tool search unless an
	 * entry starts with `mcp__`; then only matching MCP tools are kept. An empty
	 * list, like `noTools: "all"`, disables MCP tools too.
	 *
	 * A list of only `+name` and `-name` entries is not an allowlist: it adds tools
	 * to or removes them from the default selection, like the `defaultTools` setting.
	 * These entries take exact names. Mixing them with plain entries throws.
	 */
	tools?: string[];
	/**
	 * Optional denylist of tool names or patterns to disable. Applies after `tools` when both are
	 * provided, MCP tools included.
	 */
	excludeTools?: string[];
	/** Custom tools to register (in addition to built-in tools). */
	customTools?: ToolDefinition[];

	/** Resource loader. When omitted, DefaultResourceLoader is used. */
	resourceLoader?: ResourceLoader;

	/** Session manager. Default: SessionManager.create(cwd) */
	sessionManager?: SessionManager;

	/** Settings manager. Default: SettingsManager.create(cwd, agentDir) */
	settingsManager?: SettingsManager;
	/** Session start event metadata for extension runtime startup. */
	sessionStartEvent?: SessionStartEvent;
}

/** Result from createAgentSession */
export interface CreateAgentSessionResult {
	/** The created session */
	session: AgentSession;
	/** Extensions result (for UI context setup in interactive mode) */

/**
 * Create an AgentSession with the specified options.
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * // Minimal - uses defaults
 * const { session } = await createAgentSession();
 *
 * // With explicit model
 * import { getModel } from '@earendil-works/pi-ai';
 * const { session } = await createAgentSession({
 *   model: getModel('anthropic', 'claude-opus-4-5'),
 *   thinkingLevel: 'high',
 * });
 *
 * // Continue previous session
 * const { session, modelFallbackMessage } = await createAgentSession({
 *   continueSession: true,

 *
 * // Full control
 * const loader = new DefaultResourceLoader({
 *   cwd: process.cwd(),
 *   agentDir: getAgentDir(),
 *   settingsManager: 
... [opts: 30000 of 34172 chars shown. The whole value is still in the REPL under this key — slice or search it there; do not re-read or re-run it] ...
ls) : undefined;
	if (toolListError) throw new Error(`Invalid tools option: ${toolListError}`);
	const defaultToolNames = options.noTools ? [] : (settingsManager.getDefaultTools() ?? DEFAULT_TOOL_NAMES);
	// A `tools` list of only `+name`/`-name` entries changes the default selection instead of
	// replacing it, like the `defaultTools` setting.
	const toolModifiers = options.tools?.some(isToolModifier) ? options.tools : undefined;
	const selectedToolNames = toolModifiers ? applyToolModifiers(defaultToolNames, toolModifiers) : options.tools;
	const allowedToolNames = toolModifiers
		? options.noTools === "all"
			? selectedToolNames
			: undefined
		: (options.tools ?? (options.noTools === "all" ? [] : undefined));
	const excludedToolNames = options.excludeTools;
	const isExcludedTool = excludedToolNames ? createToolNameMatcher(excludedToolNames) : undefined;
	const initialActiveToolNames = (selectedToolNames ?? defaultToolNames).filter((name) => !isExcludedTool?.(name));

	// Create convertToLlm wrapper that filters images if blockImages is enabled (defense-in-depth)
	const convertToLlmWithBlockImages = (messages: AgentMessage[]): Message[] => {
		const converted = convertToLlm(messages);
		// Check setting dynamically so mid-session changes take effect
		if (!settingsManager.getBlockImages()) {
			return converted;
		}
		// Filter out ImageContent from all messages, replacing with text placeholder
		return converted.map((msg) => {
			if (msg.role === "user" || msg.role === "toolResult") {
				const content = msg.content;
				if (Array.isArray(content)) {
					const hasImages = content.some((c) => c.type === "image");
					if (hasImages) {
						const filteredContent = content
							.map((c) =>
								c.type === "image" ? { type: "text" as const, text: "Image reading is disabled." } : c,
							)
							.filter(
								(c, i, arr) =>
									// Dedupe consecutive "Image reading is disabled." texts
									!(
										c.type === "text" &&
										c.text === "Image reading is disabled." &&
										i > 0 &&
										arr[i - 1].type === "text" &&
										(arr[i - 1] as { type: "text"; text: string }).text === "Image reading is disabled."
									),
							);
						return { ...msg, content: filteredContent };
					}
				}
			}
			return msg;
		});
	};

	const extensionRunnerRef: { current?: ExtensionRunner } = {};
	const cacheWarmer = new CacheWarmer(
		modelRuntime,
		sessionManager,
		() => settingsManager.getCacheWarmingMode(),
		async (event) => extensionRunnerRef.current?.emitCacheWarmingDecision(event) ?? event.action,
	);
	const buildRequestOptions = (options: ModelsSimpleStreamOptions = {}): ModelsSimpleStreamOptions => {
		const providerRetrySettings = settingsManager.getProviderRetrySettings();
		const httpIdleTimeoutMs = settingsManager.getHttpIdleTimeoutMs();
		const effectiveTimeoutMs = httpIdleTimeoutMs === 0 ? 2147483647 : httpIdleTimeoutMs;
		const headerRunner = extensionRunnerRef.current;
		return {
			...options,
			timeoutMs: options.timeoutMs ?? providerRetrySettings.timeoutMs ?? effectiveTimeoutMs,
			websocketConnectTimeoutMs: options.websocketConnectTimeoutMs ?? settingsManager.getWebSocketConnectTimeoutMs(),
			maxRetries: options.maxRetries ?? providerRetrySettings.maxRetries,
			maxRetryDelayMs: options.maxRetryDelayMs ?? providerRetrySettings.maxRetryDelayMs,
			// Replaces the agent loop's default identity; read per request so telemetry changes apply at once.
			identity: getClientIdentity(settingsManager),
			transformHeaders: async (headers) =>
				headerRunner?.hasHandlers("before_provider_headers")
					? headerRunner.emitBeforeProviderHeaders(headers)
					: headers,
		};
	};
	// Warm only requests for the selected model. Requests a virtual selection routed, or that an
	// extension redirected, may not be repeated by the next request, so warming them could be wasted.
	const cacheContextIsCurrent = (requestModel: Model<any>) => {
		const messages = agent.state.messages;
		return () => {
			const currentModel = agent.state.model;
			const currentMessages = agent.state.messages;
			return (
				currentModel.provider === requestModel.provider &&
				currentModel.id === requestModel.id &&
				messages.length <= currentMessages.length &&
				messages.every((message, index) => currentMessages[index] === message)
			);
		};
	};
	const transformProviderPayload = async (payload: unknown) => {
		const runner = extensionRunnerRef.current;
		if (!runner?.hasHandlers("before_provider_request")) return payload;
		return runner.emitBeforeProviderRequest(payload);
	};
	const handleProviderResponse: NonNullable<ModelsSimpleStreamOptions["onResponse"]> = async (response) => {
		const runner = extensionRunnerRef.current;
		if (!runner?.hasHandlers("after_provider_response")) return;
		await runner.emit({
			type: "after_provider_response",
			status: response.status,
			headers: response.headers,
		});
	};
	const handleProviderStreamEvent: NonNullable<ModelsSimpleStreamOptions["onProviderStreamEvent"]> = async (
		data,
		model,
	) => {
		const runner = extensionRunnerRef.current;
		if (!runner?.hasHandlers("provider_stream_event")) return;
		await runner.emit({
			data,
			type: "provider_stream_event",
			provider: model.provider,
			api: model.api,
			model: model.id,
		});
	};

	const agent = new Agent({
		initialState: {
			systemPrompt: "",
			model,
			thinkingLevel,
			tools: [],
			messages: existingSession.messages,
		},
		convertToLlm: convertToLlmWithBlockImages,
		streamFn: async (model, context, options) => {
			const requestOptions = buildRequestOptions(options);
			// Compaction and summaries use their own routing ids; only session requests
			// replace the cache entry, so warming restarts from them. Keep warming while
			// the current transcript still extends the request's prefix. Agent state may
			// shallow-copy the messages array or refresh the model object without changing
			// the provider request, so top-level object identity is not a valid cache key.
			if (options?.sessionId === sessionManager.getSessionId()) {
				cacheWarmer.start({ model, context, options: requestOptions }, cacheContextIsCurrent(model));
			}
			return modelRuntime.streamSimple(model, context, requestOptions);
		},
		onPayload: transformProviderPayload,
		onResponse: handleProviderResponse,
		onProviderStreamEvent: handleProviderStreamEvent,
		sessionId: sessionManager.getSessionId(),
		transformContext: async (messages) => {
			const runner = extensionRunnerRef.current;
			if (!runner) return messages;
			return runner.emitContext(messages);
		},
		steeringMode: settingsManager.getSteeringMode(),
		followUpMode: settingsManager.getFollowUpMode(),
		transport: settingsManager.getTransport(),
		thinkingBudgets: settingsManager.getThinkingBudgets(),
		maxRetryDelayMs: settingsManager.getProviderRetrySettings().maxRetryDelayMs,
	});
	// This stream resolves auth through modelRuntime, so summaries must not pre-resolve it (#11520).
	markRuntimeStreamFunction(agent.streamFunction, modelRuntime);

	// Restore missing settings metadata for older sessions.
	if (hasExistingSession) {
		if (!hasThinkingEntry) {
			sessionManager.appendThinkingLevelChange(thinkingLevel);
		}
	} else {
		// Save initial model and thinking level for new sessions so they can be restored on resume
		if (model) {
			sessionManager.appendModelChange(model.provider, model.id);
		}
		sessionManager.appendThinkingLevelChange(thinkingLevel);
	}
